project.name: unihack8
project.description: Hackathon mobile app for Timișoara (Connected Communities): Spring Boot API + Supabase + Expo app with events and QR reliability points, places map, live STPT transit, routing and an AI guide.

tour.title: Project Vision and Plan
tour.description: The README is only a title, so the real starting point is AGENTS.md, which states the Connected Communities problem, the team rules (tests for every change, keep DOCS.md and the knowledge graph current) and the core idea: a Timișoara map with places, live STPT transit, directions, an AI guide and community events with reliability points. PLAN.md turns that vision into numbered tasks across backend, data/AI services and mobile tracks, so you can see what already exists and what comes next.

tour.title: Documentation and API Contract
tour.description: DOCS.md is the living map of the system: architecture, backend configuration, run instructions and every feature added so far, updated with each change. docs/API.md is the contract between the mobile app and the backend (conventions, paged and error shapes, shared objects and endpoints), so the Java code later in the tour simply implements what it promises. .mcp.json registers the hosted Supabase MCP server that AI tooling uses to inspect and migrate the database.

tour.title: Profiles and Events Schema
tour.description: The data model lives in Supabase Postgres. Migration 1 creates public.profiles, one row per Supabase auth user with a case-insensitive unique username, filled automatically by the on_auth_user_created trigger. Migration 2 builds on it with public.events for both user-created (USER) and imported (EXTERNAL) events, using check constraints so invalid sources, coordinates or prices can never reach the map.
tour.languageLesson: A Postgres trigger on auth.users lets the database create the app-side profile row the moment someone signs up, so the backend never has to remember to do it.

tour.title: Participation and Reliability
tour.description: This migration models the project's signature feature. event_participants joins users to events with a status lifecycle (JOINED, ATTENDED, NO_SHOW, CANCELLED) and the QR token used for check-in, while reliability_log records every signed point change as an audit trail. Together they make reliability points explainable rather than a single opaque counter.
tour.languageLesson: An append-only log table like reliability_log is a common SQL pattern: each change is stored as a row and totals are derived from it, so history is never lost.

tour.title: Places Table and Schema Checks
tour.description: Migration 4 adds public.places for restaurants, cafes and other points of interest imported from OpenStreetMap, unique by osm_id so re-imports update rows instead of duplicating them. schema_checks.sql is a self-rolling-back PL/pgSQL block that tests the rules from Steps 3-5, so it can run safely against the shared Supabase database without leaving data behind.

tour.title: Spring Boot Entry and Settings
tour.description: BackendApplication bootstraps the Spring Boot API that sits between the app and the database from the previous steps. SupabaseProperties binds the Supabase URL and HS256 JWT secret and derives the token issuer, TimeConfig exposes a shared UTC Clock so time logic is testable, and application.properties tells Hibernate to only validate against the Supabase migrations and binds the server on 0.0.0.0:8080 so phones on the LAN can reach it.
tour.languageLesson: Java records annotated with @ConfigurationProperties give immutable, validated config objects, and injecting a Clock bean instead of calling Instant.now() lets tests freeze time.

tour.title: Security and the Current User
tour.description: SecurityConfig makes the backend a stateless JWT resource server: Supabase access tokens are validated with the secret and issuer from Step 6, public GET routes stay open, and everything else requires a token. CurrentUser reads the token's sub claim to give services the caller's UUID, and the JSON entry point and access-denied handler make 401 and 403 answers use the same error format as the rest of the API.
tour.languageLesson: In modern Spring Security you declare a SecurityFilterChain bean; configuring oauth2ResourceServer with a JWT decoder means every request is authenticated before any controller runs.

tour.title: One Error Format Everywhere
tour.description: ErrorCode is one of the most depended-on files in the backend: an enum listing every API error with its HTTP status, from validation and auth to QR check-in and rate limiting. Code throws ApiException with a code, GlobalExceptionHandler catches it (plus validation and malformed-body errors), and ErrorResponseFactory builds the ErrorResponse record, the single error JSON shape promised in docs/API.md and shared with the security handlers from Step 7.
tour.languageLesson: @RestControllerAdvice with @ExceptionHandler methods centralises error handling, so controllers just throw and never build error bodies themselves.

tour.title: Paging and Geo Building Blocks
tour.description: PageParams enforces the API paging rules (page from 0, default size 20, capped at 100) and PageResponse is the matching generic list shape. GeoPoint is the most imported file in the whole backend: places, transit and routing all describe locations with it. BoundingBox parses the bbox=minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat viewport parameter, and GeoParsing turns malformed coordinates into 400 VALIDATION_FAILED errors through the system from Step 8.
tour.languageLesson: Java records can validate their fields in a compact constructor, and a generic record like PageResponse<T> gives one reusable, type-safe wrapper for any list.

tour.title: Build and Test Foundation
tour.description: build.gradle targets Java 21 and Spring Boot with JPA, Security and Validation, and application-local.properties.example lists the Supabase URL, JWT secret and pooler connection each developer fills into a git-ignored local profile. Tests use a separate application.properties with in-memory H2 in PostgreSQL mode and a fake secret; JwtTestTokens signs Supabase-shaped tokens and the test-only TestProbeController exposes probe endpoints so the security and error rules can be verified before any feature exists.
tour.languageLesson: The Gradle wrapper (gradlew plus gradle-wrapper.properties) downloads a pinned Gradle version on first run, so every teammate builds the same way without a global install.

tour.title: Places: Importing OpenStreetMap
tour.description: The first feature fills the places table from Step 5. PlaceCategory defines the app categories and which OSM tags select them, OverpassClientImpl downloads Timișoara from the Overpass API (falling back to another server when one is busy), and OsmElementMapperImpl turns raw elements into rows (position from node or way centre, ATM names from operator or brand). PlaceImportServiceImpl downloads outside a transaction, then de-duplicates, upserts by osmId and deletes vanished places in one transaction, and PlaceImportRunner triggers it at startup when places.import.enabled=true.

tour.title: Places: Searching the Map
tour.description: Place is the JPA entity over the places table. PlaceController exposes GET /places with category, viewport, name and near-me filters plus GET /places/{id}, and PlaceServiceImpl answers them using the GeoPoint and BoundingBox helpers from Step 9. PlaceSpecifications composes the filters as JPA Specifications (category IN, bbox BETWEEN, escaped case-insensitive name LIKE), and PlaceMapperImpl copies entities into DTOs while whitelisting which OSM tags are public.
tour.languageLesson: JPA Specifications are small predicate builders you combine with and(), so optional filters are added only when the request contains them instead of writing one query per combination.

tour.title: Live Transit: Cache and STPT Client
tour.description: Live transit depends on undocumented STPT live-site endpoints, so it starts with resilience. StaleCache is a generic, thread-safe TTL cache: fresh entries are served directly, expired ones are reloaded, and if a reload fails the last known value is returned and flagged stale. StptProperties binds the stpt.* settings (timeouts, user agent, per-data-type TTLs), StptClientConfig builds the RestClient, and StptClientImpl leniently parses responses into raw Stpt* records.
tour.languageLesson: Generics such as StaleCache<K, V> let one carefully written, thread-safe class serve stops, routes, vehicles and alerts without duplicating cache logic.

tour.title: Live Transit: Service and Endpoints
tour.description: The project keeps two DTO families: raw STPT records mirroring the upstream format and clean API records matching docs/API.md. TransitMapperImpl bridges them by hand, splitting route ends, classifying vehicle types and converting local Timișoara arrival times to UTC even across midnight. TransitServiceImpl, the file with the widest reach in the backend, fetches through the client from Step 13, caches with stale fallback and maps the results; TransitController exposes the public /transit endpoints, and TransitSummaryResponse powers the 'last tram at this hour' idea from Step 1.

tour.title: Our Own Routing Server: OTP
tour.description: Directions need a real journey planner, so the project runs its own OpenTripPlanner 2 server. get-data.sh downloads the STPT GTFS timetable (with a Mobility Database mirror fallback) and the Romania OSM extract, then crops it to the Timișoara bounding box with osmium. docker-compose.yml runs OTP 2.7.0 as a one-off otp-build service that builds graph.obj and an otp service that serves it on host port 8081, and infra/otp/README.md explains the three commands to download, build and serve.
tour.languageLesson: Docker Compose profiles let a heavy, one-off job (building the routing graph) live in the same file as the long-running server without starting every time you run docker compose up.

tour.title: Routing: Planning a Trip
tour.description: RoutingController exposes the authenticated GET /routes/plan endpoint, parsing from/to coordinates into GeoPoints and passing a TravelMode (WALK or TRANSIT) and optional departure time. RoutingServiceImpl asks OTP for itineraries and picks the earliest-arriving one rather than trusting OTP's order. Its fallbacks are deliberate: WALK with OTP down returns a straight-line walking estimate, TRANSIT with OTP down returns 503, and a TRANSIT request with no trip falls back to walking; RoutePlanResponse carries a fallback flag so the app can tell the difference.

tour.title: Routing: Talking to OTP over GraphQL
tour.description: OtpGraphQlClient implements the OtpClient interface by POSTing a planConnection GraphQL query to OTP's /otp/gtfs/v1 endpoint on the server from Step 15: a direct walk only for WALK, or walk access plus transit for TRANSIT. OtpProperties (defaulting to localhost:8081) and OtpClientConfig give the RestClient short timeouts so a slow OTP cannot hang the API, and any transport or GraphQL error becomes OtpUnavailableException, the signal RoutingServiceImpl uses for its fallbacks. OtpPlanResult is a nested record tree mirroring the GraphQL response.
tour.languageLesson: GraphQL can answer with HTTP 200 even when a query fails, listing the problems in an errors array, so a client must check that array and not just the status code.

tour.title: Routing: Shaping the Answer
tour.description: RoutePlanMapperImpl turns OTP itineraries into the app's RoutePlanResponse: it detects the overall mode, rounds minutes and meters, emits UTC times and normalises each leg to WALK, TRAM, TROLLEYBUS or BUS, keeping line and headsign only for vehicle legs. It also builds the fallback walking estimate from Step 16 from straight-line distance times a detour factor at 4.8 km/h, and PolylineEncoder handles the Google encoded polyline that each RouteLegResponse carries for the map to draw.
tour.languageLesson: The encoded polyline format stores coordinate deltas at 1e5 precision as zig-zag, 5-bit chunks of ASCII, shrinking a long path to a short string that map libraries decode directly.

tour.title: Feature Tests with Recorded Answers
tour.description: Every external source is tested without the network. StptClientImplTest replays saved STPT responses and TransitServiceImplTest checks caching and stale fallback with a hand-advanced clock, while plan-transit.json is a recorded OTP answer for a real Timișoara trip used by OtpGraphQlClientTest and the mapper tests. RoutingServiceImplTest pins down the rules from Step 16, including picking the earliest arrival rather than OTP's order and the walking fallbacks.

tour.title: The Expo Mobile App
tour.description: On the client side, _layout.jsx is the Expo Router root with the status bar and native Stack navigator, and index.jsx is the Discover screen rendering a map centred on Timișoara. map.js keeps the TIMISOARA_CENTER coordinates and region math out of the UI, and api.js is the minimal HTTP client that reads the backend URL from EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL to reach the endpoints built in the previous steps. package.json pins Expo SDK 54, React Native 0.81, expo-router and react-native-maps.
tour.languageLesson: Expo Router uses file-based routing: _layout.jsx wraps every screen in its folder and index.jsx becomes the default route. Only EXPO_PUBLIC_ variables reach app code, and they are inlined at build time, so never put secrets in them.
